A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same λ-Orthogonality research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I are readable and can be reliably matched despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, representation-compatibility, and partial-backfilling experiments, including downstream evaluations and ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original retrieval, compatibility, backfilling, and appendix ablation results. These qualify as original empirical results even though they are unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: The backward and forward transformations, λ-orthogonality regularizer, contrastive objective, total training loss, and class-mean backfilling procedure remain unchanged. The correction to Definition 3.1 does not modify the reported algorithm or losses.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the MNIST illustration, ImageNet1K experiments, CUB200/CIFAR100/Places365/Flowers102 downstream evaluations, Places205-to-Places365 update, and CLIP/DINOv2 update scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: FCT and FastFill remain the retrieval comparators, with FCT alone retained in the CLIP/DINOv2 comparisons. SO and SRIP remain the regularization comparators. The newly cited CL2R work is not added to any evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Class splits, model configurations, query/gallery construction, self-match exclusion, CMC-Top1/mAP metrics, and backfilling evaluation remain unchanged. The empirical compatibility criterion in Eq. 11 and reported adapter-training settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The λ sweep, regularizer-weight sensitivity comparison, loss-component ablations, and MSE-versus-cosine backfilling analysis are retained unchanged. The SO/SRIP comparison moves from Appendix F to Appendix E without adding or revising an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Neither introduces a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 14 matched tables retain their numerical results and comparator rows, and the figures retain their plotted findings. For example, Table 2 retains the adapted-model CMC-Top1 scores of 75.44 on CUB and 78.23 on CIFAR100; v1 Table 13 and v2 Table 10 contain identical regularizer-comparison results.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Eq. 1, changes the different-class lower bound from new-model distances d(h_i^t,h_j^t) to old-model distances d(h_i^k,h_j^k). Cross-model terms are also consistently written as d(h_i^t,h_j^k). This substantively corrects the formal compatibility definition; the remaining mathematical formulations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about representation compatibility, geometry-preserving downstream adaptation, contrastive alignment, and efficient backfilling. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the stability–plasticity tradeoff, CLIP results, and loss contributions are retained. Appendix I preserves the same limitations concerning lower-quality updated models and manual λ selection; relocating the regularizer discussion adds no new interpretation.

D1.justification: The same pretrained-model sources, dimensionality handling, optimization details, hyperparameters, and code-access information are disclosed. The repository and training-resource link targets are identical; displayed punctuation changes do not alter access.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds CL2R: Compatible Lifelong Learning Representations as an example of architecture-based compatibility work, with a new reference 40. Other bibliography changes update existing works' publication metadata without substantively changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited tense, capitalization, punctuation, and bibliographic edits, adds acknowledgments, and replaces the preprint notice with a NeurIPS 2025 conference line. It also moves the regularizer-weight discussion from Appendix F to Appendix E while retaining the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is resized and placed beside its Appendix E discussion. Several appendix displays are relocated, including v1 Table 13 becoming v2 Table 10, and table numbering and references are corrected. The displayed scientific content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects Eq. 1 so different-class separation is benchmarked against the old model, consistent with the accompanying backward-compatibility explanation. Grouping the regularizer comparison in Appendix E and correcting table references also improves organization. These are limited improvements in formal clarity and presentation; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
